binders: N is an arbitrary natural number and is the common matrix and vector dimension.
uLow, uFma, and u are arbitrary real numbers.
q, n, and bdim are arbitrary natural numbers; n is a count parameter distinct from the dimension N.
A, L, U, ΔF, ΔL, ΔU, and M are arbitrary real N-by-N matrices, represented as functions Fin N → Fin N → ℝ.
x, y, and rhs are arbitrary real N-vectors, represented as functions Fin N → ℝ.
hypotheses: The exact matrix identity LU = A + ΔF holds.
The exact vector identity (L + ΔL)y = rhs holds.
The exact vector identity (U + ΔU)x = y holds.
For every i,j ∈ Fin N, |ΔF_ij| ≤ αM_ij.
For every i,j ∈ Fin N, |(LΔU)_ij| ≤ γ_n(u)M_ij.
For every i,j ∈ Fin N, |(ΔL U)_ij| ≤ γ_n(u)M_ij.
For every i,j ∈ Fin N, |(ΔL ΔU)_ij| ≤ γ_n(u)²M_ij.
conclusions: There exists a real N-by-N matrix ΔA, chosen after all preceding data and hypotheses and therefore permitted to depend on them, such that (A + ΔA)x = rhs exactly.
The same ΔA satisfies, for every i,j ∈ Fin N, |ΔA_ij| ≤ (α + 2γ_n(u) + γ_n(u)²)M_ij.
mathematical_definitions: Write I_N = Fin N = {0,…,N-1}. For matrices B and C, (BC)_ij = Σ_(k∈I_N) B_ik C_kj. For a vector z, (Bz)_i = Σ_(j∈I_N) B_ij z_j. Matrix addition is entrywise.
For m ∈ ℕ and v ∈ ℝ, define γ_m(v) = ((m : ℝ)v)/(1 - (m : ℝ)v).
Natural subtraction is truncated: q ⊖ 1 = max(q - 1,0) and n ⊖ bdim = max(n - bdim,0).
Define α = 2uLow + uLow² + max(γ_(q⊖1)(uFma) + γ_((n⊖bdim)+1)(u) + γ_(q⊖1)(uFma)γ_((n⊖bdim)+1)(u), γ_bdim(u))(1 + uLow)².
Define the final scalar coefficient C = α + 2γ_n(u) + γ_n(u)²; the final bound is |ΔA_ij| ≤ CM_ij.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every dimension N, all stated real parameters, count parameters, real N-by-N matrices, and real N-vectors, suppose LU equals A + ΔF exactly, the perturbed lower-factor equation (L + ΔL)y = rhs holds exactly, and the perturbed upper-factor equation (U + ΔU)x = y holds exactly. Suppose additionally that ΔF, LΔU, ΔL U, and ΔL ΔU satisfy the four stated entrywise absolute-value bounds relative to the raw entries M_ij. Then there is an N-by-N real perturbation ΔA, potentially depending on this particular x, y, rhs, and all other supplied data, for which x solves (A + ΔA)x = rhs exactly and whose entries obey |ΔA_ij| ≤ (α + 2γ_n(u) + γ_n(u)²)M_ij.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: N may be zero. When N = 0, all index sets are empty, all entrywise bounds are vacuous, all vector equalities are equalities between empty functions, and the conclusion is trivial.
No positivity, smallness, or unit-roundoff assumptions are imposed on uLow, uFma, or u.

No denominator condition such as 1 - (m : ℝ)v ≠ 0 is imposed. Lean's real division is total, so γ_m(v) remains a term even when the denominator is zero rather than being excluded as mathematically undefined.
No assumptions q ≥ 1 or n ≥ bdim are present. Thus q - 1 and n - bdim are truncated natural differences.
No relationship is imposed among N, q, n, and bdim.

M is arbitrary and is not assumed entrywise nonnegative. Every right-hand side uses M_ij itself, not |M_ij|. If one of these products is negative, the corresponding absolute-value hypothesis is impossible and the implication is vacuously true for that data.
The scalar coefficients α and γ_n(u) are not assumed nonnegative.
The bounds are entrywise scalar bounds. No matrix norm or vector norm occurs.
L and U are not asserted to be triangular, invertible, or nonsingular, and no structural relation between M and L or U is encoded.

All equations and operations are exact over ℝ. The proposition does not encode floating-point operations, an algorithm, computed-versus-exact values, or any rounding process beyond the displayed algebraic assumptions.
The existential ΔA is selected after x, y, rhs, and all hypotheses. The proposition does not assert one perturbation that works uniformly for every right-hand side or solution vector.
The proposition neither specifies a formula for ΔA nor asserts uniqueness.
